answer: Shared-Resource Ledger. Each identity must hold a rotating slice of a scarce, non-transferable resource—compute-hours or a physical dock slot on the wharf—reassigned each epoch. Clones that wander between addresses must reacquire a slice at rising auction prices, and any slice left idle decays. Registration also demands a unique signed fable-history hash that cannot be copied without paying the prior holder's exit price. A marginal clone thus costs more in auction fees and decay than it earns.
